purpose: Review a user-supplied extraction; no new inference, coefficient fitting or production benchmark import.

verified_dataset_conditions.test: Speed: output tokens per second on a short chat (median of 3 after a warm-up). Memory: peak during a 4,096-token prompt. Quality: how often the version picks the same next word as a near-lossless 8-bit copy (top-1 match), plus 10 short questions with one right answer. mlx 0.32.4.
verified_dataset_conditions.source_note: Entered from the factory report as posted on the day; the full result files are on the Mac mini. Rows marked 'about' will be exact after the next run.
verified_dataset_conditions.takeaway: the standard 4-bit build runs well on a 32 GB+ Mac; neither tested change helped.

verified_dataset_conditions.test: draft-ahead (speculative) decoding: the small mlx-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-MLX-4bit guesses 4 words at a time and Qwen 3.8 27B checks them in one pass; 76% of guesses were kept. 200 GSM8K problems, the same for both, measured with mlx-lm in Python, greedy, thinking off, up to 1,024 tokens. The standard build was timed again in the same sitting, with serving paused (this sitting's standard speed is lower than the 35.7 tok/s chat test above, which used a different prompt and length).
verified_dataset_conditions.takeaway: draft-ahead made Qwen 3.8 27B 81% faster with the same right answers and only 3% more memory, the first speed-up to beat a standard build on this page.
verified_dataset_conditions.caution: Important: this gain was measured greedy with thinking off. When our Mac app served it live at its default settings (temperature 0.6, thinking on), we did not see the speed-up, so the app has draft-ahead turned off again while we find out why. Do not expect this speed from Smarty Pants today.

rows.label: Standard 4-bit + guess 4 words ahead (test only, off in the app)
rows.why: 81% faster, same right answers, 3% more memory (in this test setup; not yet in the live app)

verified_dataset_conditions.test: the full GSM8K test (1,319 problems), the same for both, served the way Smarty Pants serves it: thinking off, greedy, up to 1,024 tokens. Better needs answers as good (95% interval of the accuracy change above -2 points) plus at least 10% faster or 10% less memory. In the Mac app's own code, at temperature 0.6 with thinking on, the smaller build also ran faster: 20.3 vs 17.6 tok/s.
verified_dataset_conditions.takeaway: the smaller tuned build gives the same answers (94.6% vs 94.8%, no real difference) while running 15% faster on 15% less memory, so it fits more Macs.
verified_dataset_conditions.credit: the 3.80-bits-per-weight DWQ build is by AtomicChat ([AtomicChat/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-AD-3.80bpw-DWQ-13.7GB](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-AD-3.80bpw-DWQ-13.7GB), revision 9fa7ab0); we tested it.

rows.label: AtomicChat 3.80-bit DWQ (tuned to copy the full model)
rows.why: 15% faster and 15% less memory, answers as good (-1.2 to +0.8 points)
